samasa.vigraha: वैष्णव्याः चक्रं वैष्णवीचक्रम्; तेन भिन्नः, तस्य
samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (वैष्णवीचक्र)
samasa.literal: of the one split by Vaiṣṇavī’s discus
samasa.sense: of Raktabīja, gashed by the discus of 8.47

samasa.vigraha: रुधिरस्य स्रावः रुधिरस्रावः; रुधिरस्रावात् सम्भवः येषां तैः
samasa.literal: by those whose origin is from the flow of blood

morph.note: Past passive participle of वि + √आप्: ‘reached through, pervaded’. With the instrumental agent महासुरैः it makes a passive sentence: ‘the world was filled by great asuras’.
भिन्न is the past participle of √भिद् ‘split’, with -न instead of -त. The genitive names whose blood it was.

mantras.anvaya: वैष्णवीचक्रभिन्नस्य (तस्य) रुधिरस्रावसम्भवैः तत्प्रमाणैः महासुरैः सहस्रशः जगत् व्याप्तम् (आसीत्)।
mantras.lit: By great asuras of his size, born by thousands from the flow of blood of him who was split by Vaiṣṇavī’s discus, the world was filled.
mantras.tr: From the blood that streamed from him when Vaiṣṇavī’s discus split him open, great asuras of his stature were born in thousands and filled the world.

comm.t: The scale widens from the battlefield to the world (जगत्). The passive construction makes the asuras the agents and the world the thing overwhelmed.

mantras.anvaya: कौमारी शक्त्या, तथा वाराही च असिना, माहेश्वरी त्रिशूलेन रक्तबीजं महासुरं जघान।
mantras.lit: Kaumārī struck the great asura Raktabīja with the spear, and likewise Vārāhī with the sword, Māheśvarī with the trident.
mantras.tr: Kaumārī struck the great asura Raktabīja with her spear, Vārāhī with her sword, and Māheśvarī with her trident.

comm.t: Every Mother now attacks Raktabīja himself, and every blow is another wound. The verse repeats the pattern of 8.34 — three goddesses, three weapons, one verb — but now against the one enemy whose wounds multiply him.

sandhi.rule: एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि (6.1.132); अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (6.1.101)
sandhi.note: सः drops its visarga before the consonant c; च + अपि → चापि.
-āḥ before a vowel loses its visarga and the vowels stand apart (सर्वा एव); एव + अहनत् → एवाहनत्.
-aḥ before the voiced r and m becomes -o, twice.

morph.note: The classical imperfect of √हन् is अहन्. अहनत्, inflected like a thematic (a-stem) verb, is an epic (ārṣa) form; the metre needs its extra syllable (सर्वा एवाहनत् पृथक् is eight syllables, with अहन् it would be seven).
Accusative plural of the feminine ṛ-stem मातृ: मातॄः, with long ṝ (the masculine would be पितॄन्).

mantras.anvaya: सः रक्तबीजः महासुरः दैत्यः च अपि कोपसमाविष्टः गदया सर्वाः एव मातॄः पृथक् अहनत्।
mantras.lit: And he too, the Daitya, the great asura Raktabīja, possessed by rage, struck all the Mothers, each separately, with his mace.
mantras.tr: Raktabīja, the great asura, in a fury, struck back at every one of the Mothers in turn with his mace.

comm.t: The asura answers each attacker with the mace he carried from the start (8.42 गदापाणिः). पृथक् ‘separately’ shows him striking back at each of the Mothers in turn.

sandhi.type: visarga sandhi; vowel sandhi; consonant sandhi (n + ś); pūrvarūpa
sandhi.note: रक्तौघः before t → रक्तौघस्; तेन + आसन् → तेनासन्; the final n of आसन् before ś becomes the palatal ñ, and the ś after it is sounded ch (a t is inserted before ś and शश्छोऽटि applies: आसञ्छतशः); शतशः before a becomes शतशो and the a is elided (शतशोऽसुराः).

samasa.vigraha: शक्तिश्च शूलं च शक्तिशूले; शक्तिशूले आदी येषां तैः
samasa.literal: by those of which spear and trident are the first
samasa.sense: by the spears, tridents and other weapons of the Mothers
the stream that poured from his wounds

morph.note: Imperfect third plural of √अस् ‘be’ (आ-सन्), here ‘came to be, arose’.
The taddhita -धा forms adverbs of manner from numerals and quantities: बहुधा ‘in many ways’.

mantras.anvaya: बहुधा शक्तिशूलादिभिः आहतस्य तस्य यः वै रक्तौघः भुवि पपात, तेन शतशः असुराः आसन्।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (यः … रक्तौघः पपात) and its correlative main clause (तेन … असुराः आसन्).
mantras.lit: The flood of blood which fell indeed on the ground from him, struck many times by spears, tridents and the rest — from it asuras came into being by hundreds.
mantras.tr: Struck again and again by spears, tridents and the rest, he poured a flood of blood upon the ground, and from it asuras arose in their hundreds.

comm.t: The narrator presses the point once more: the Mothers’ weapons cannot end him, because every wound feeds the army they are fighting.

samasa.vigraha: असुरस्य असृक् असुरासृक्; असुरासृजः सम्भूताः, तैः
samasa.type: pañcamī tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (असुरासृक्)
samasa.sense: the doubles born of Raktabīja’s blood

morph.note: असृज् ‘blood’ (n.) appears in a compound with its final j turned to k before the s of सम्भूत. The same noun closes the chapter (8.63 असृङ्मद-).
Perfect of √गम् with आ: reduplicated ज-ग्म्- (the root vowel drops before the ending -उः). भयम् आजग्मुः ‘they came into fear’.

mantras.anvaya: तैः च असुरासृक्सम्भूतैः असुरैः सकलं जगत् व्याप्तम् आसीत्; ततः देवाः उत्तमं भयम् आजग्मुः।
mantras.lit: And by those asuras sprung from the asura’s blood the whole world was filled; then the gods fell into the utmost fear.
mantras.tr: The whole world was overrun by those asuras born of the asura’s blood, and the gods were seized with the greatest fear.

comm.t: The crisis of the chapter. For the first time in the battle the gods, who have been watching, are afraid: the Mothers’ victories have become a defeat. The turn comes in the next verse, with Caṇḍikā’s command.
